# layout


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Component styles set internal padding. Layout attributes on the parent
control spacing between child elements. Each FastHTML constructor
returns a `Div` with the matching HTML attribute:

- `Stack` sets `stack` for a vertical column.
- `Cluster` sets `cluster` for a wrapping row.
- `Grid` sets `grid` for adaptive equal-width columns.
- `Flow` sets `flow` for document spacing.

Put any of those attributes directly on a semantic element such as
`Section(..., stack=True)` to match the same CSS rules without an extra
wrapper.

``` python
from fasthtml.common import Article, Header, Section, Ul, Li, to_xml
from answerui.demo import demo
```

## Stack

`Stack` arranges its children in a flex column and stretches them across
the available width. Setting `gap` on the parent puts space only between
adjacent children, avoiding a trailing margin after the last child. The
default gap is `--space`.

Every layout constructor accepts CSS lengths or token references (such
as `'var(--space-2)'`) for its sizing options. Layout rules stay in the
stylesheet. `_layout` prepends those custom properties to any `style`
string the caller passes:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Stack

``` python
def Stack(
    *c, gap:NoneType=None, **attrs
):
```

*A vertical group with space between its children*

None of these children has a margin. The `[stack]` container sets the
spacing between them:

``` python
Stack.demo()
```

``` html
<div stack>
  <h2>Account</h2>
  <p>Manage your profile and preferences.</p>
<small>Changes apply to this workspace.</small></div>
```

For a tighter gap, pass `gap`. The constructor sets it as `--gap` on the
same `div`, with no extra wrapper or styling class:

``` python
to_xml(Stack(P('Ada Lovelace'), Small('Workspace owner'), gap='var(--space-2)'))
```

    '<div stack style="--gap: var(--space-2);">\n  <p>Ada Lovelace</p>\n<small>Workspace owner</small></div>\n'

You can also put `stack=True` on a semantic element. Here the `section`
keeps its tag while matching the `[stack]` rule with the default
`--space` gap:

``` python
demo(Section(H2('Profile'), P('Visible to the rest of your team.'), stack=True))
```

``` html
<section stack>
  <h2>Profile</h2>
  <p>Visible to the rest of your team.</p>
</section>
```

## Cluster

`Cluster` arranges short items such as tags or metadata in a wrapping
flex row. Each child stays at its natural width and aligns centrally on
the cross axis. The `--gap` custom property (default `--space`) sets
both row and column spacing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Cluster

``` python
def Cluster(
    *c, gap:NoneType=None, **attrs
):
```

*A row of naturally sized children that wraps to fit*

``` python
Cluster.demo()
```

``` html
<div cluster style="--gap: var(--space-2);">
<code>FastHTML</code><code>htmx</code><code>semantic HTML</code><code>CSS</code></div>
```

Inside a narrow container, the same cluster wraps without a media
breakpoint even on a wide viewport:

``` python
demo(Div(_cluster_example(), style='max-inline-size: 14rem; border: 1px dashed var(--n-1)'))
```

``` html
<div style="max-inline-size: 14rem; border: 1px dashed var(--n-1)">
  <div cluster style="--gap: var(--space-2);">
<code>FastHTML</code><code>htmx</code><code>semantic HTML</code><code>CSS</code>  </div>
</div>
```

Pass `grow=True` on one child in a `Cluster` to fill the remaining width
and push later items to the far edge. Because `[grow]` also sets
`min-inline-size: 0`, a long name beside action controls wraps instead
of pushing the actions out of the row:

``` python
demo(Cluster(Code('FastHTML'), Stack(P('Ada Lovelace'), Small('Owner'), gap='0', grow=True), Code('Edit'), Code('Remove')))
```

``` html
<div cluster>
<code>FastHTML</code>  <div stack grow style="--gap: 0;">
    <p>Ada Lovelace</p>
<small>Owner</small>  </div>
<code>Edit</code><code>Remove</code></div>
```

## Grid

Unlike `Cluster`, `Grid` places its children in equal-width columns. It
fits as many columns as the container allows at a minimum width of
`16rem` (`--grid-min`) and distributes the remaining width evenly. When
the container is narrower than `--grid-min`, a single column shrinks to
fit instead of overflowing. Pass `min_width` to override `--grid-min`
without adding media breakpoints.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Grid

``` python
def Grid(
    *c, gap:NoneType=None, min_width:NoneType=None, **attrs
):
```

*Equal-width columns whose count adapts to the available width*

Each column contains a stack with a smaller gap. Changing the grid’s
`gap` doesn’t change the stacks inside it, because each layout sets its
own `--gap`.

``` python
Grid.demo()
```

``` html
<div grid>
  <div stack style="--gap: var(--space-2);">
    <h3>Inbox</h3>
    <p>Requests waiting for a first look.</p>
  </div>
  <div stack style="--gap: var(--space-2);">
    <h3>In progress</h3>
    <p>Work the team has picked up.</p>
  </div>
  <div stack style="--gap: var(--space-2);">
    <h3>Done</h3>
    <p>Completed work, ready to share.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

`grow=True` also works inside a `Stack` to fill the remaining height. In
a grid of cards, passing `grow=True` on the card body aligns every
card’s footer to the bottom regardless of title length:

``` python
demo(Grid(Stack(P('A short title'), P('Body', grow=True), Small('Foot')), Stack(P('A title long enough that it wraps onto a second line in a narrow column'), P('Body', grow=True), Small('Foot'))), width='24rem')
```

``` html
<div grid>
  <div stack>
    <p>A short title</p>
    <p grow>Body</p>
<small>Foot</small>  </div>
  <div stack>
    <p>A title long enough that it wraps onto a second line in a narrow column</p>
    <p grow>Body</p>
<small>Foot</small>  </div>
</div>
```

## Lists

Interface groups such as member lists or link menus can still use
semantic `Ul` or `Ol` elements. Putting `stack=True`, `cluster=True`, or
`grid=True` on a `ul` or `ol` clears the default list markers and
padding (`list-style: none; padding: 0`) so its `li` items lay out like
any other container.

A stacked `Ul` of names without default list markers:

``` python
demo(Ul(Li('Ada Lovelace'), Li('Grace Hopper'), Li('Alan Turing'), stack=True, cls='gap-2'))
```

``` html
<ul stack class="gap-2">
  <li>Ada Lovelace</li>
  <li>Grace Hopper</li>
  <li>Alan Turing</li>
</ul>
```

## Flow

`Flow` uses CSS grid with a default row gap of `.5em` (`--flow-space`)
for short text sections containing headings and paragraphs. Any heading
(`h1` through `h6`) after the first child has an extra `.5em` top margin
(`margin-block-start`), putting more space before a heading than after
it.

`gap` sets `--flow-space` independently of the `--gap` used by `Stack`,
`Cluster`, and `Grid`. You can nest a `Flow` with a smaller `gap`
without changing the outer `Flow`’s spacing. For full articles that also
style lists, blockquotes, code, and tables, use `prose=True`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Flow

``` python

    *c, gap:NoneType=None, **attrs
):
```

*Document flow with closer spacing after headings*

``` python
Flow.demo()
```

``` html
<div flow>
  <h2>Sharing a workspace</h2>
  <p>Invite your colleagues to work on the same projects.</p>
  <p>Everyone sees the latest changes.</p>
  <h3>Permissions</h3>
  <p>Choose who can edit and who can view.</p>
</div>
```

## Composition

The page below uses a stack to space its header, project grid, and help
text. The header has its own smaller gap and a cluster of metadata. The
article uses flow for its heading and paragraphs. Each layout spaces
only its own direct children, whatever layouts its neighbours use.

``` python
demo(Section(
    Header(H2('Workspace'), P('A shared place for the team\'s projects.'),
        Cluster(Small('3 projects'), Small('Updated today'), gap='var(--space-2)'),
        stack=True, cls='gap-2'),
    _grid_example(),
    Article(H3('Working together'), P('Pick a project to see its latest work.'),
        P('Use the inbox for requests that have not yet been assigned.'), flow=True),
    stack=True, cls='gap-8'))
```

``` html
<section stack class="gap-8">
  <header stack class="gap-2">
    <h2>Workspace</h2>
    <p>A shared place for the team's projects.</p>
    <div cluster style="--gap: var(--space-2);">
<small>3 projects</small><small>Updated today</small>    </div>
  </header>
  <div grid>
    <div stack style="--gap: var(--space-2);">
      <h3>Inbox</h3>
      <p>Requests waiting for a first look.</p>
    </div>
    <div stack style="--gap: var(--space-2);">
      <h3>In progress</h3>
      <p>Work the team has picked up.</p>
    </div>
    <div stack style="--gap: var(--space-2);">
      <h3>Done</h3>
      <p>Completed work, ready to share.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <article flow>
    <h3>Working together</h3>
    <p>Pick a project to see its latest work.</p>
    <p>Use the inbox for requests that have not yet been assigned.</p>
  </article>
</section>
```

The outer `Flow` sets a `2rem` gap around the nested `Flow`. The inner
`Flow` uses a `.25rem` gap between its two paragraphs:

``` python
demo(Flow(P('Before the nested flow.'), Flow(P('Inner one.'), P('Inner two.'), gap='.25rem'), P('After it.'), gap='2rem'))
```

``` html
<div flow style="--flow-space: 2rem;">
  <p>Before the nested flow.</p>
  <div flow style="--flow-space: .25rem;">
    <p>Inner one.</p>
    <p>Inner two.</p>
  </div>
  <p>After it.</p>
</div>
```

To change a layout default across an application, override its custom
property in the `app` CSS layer (for example,
`[cluster] { --gap: var(--space-2); }`). For a single element, pass a
spacing utility class such as `cls='gap-2'` (`.gap-0`, `.gap-1` through
`.gap-4`, `.gap-6`, `.gap-8`, `.gap-12`), pass a constructor parameter
such as `gap` for custom lengths, or set the custom property in `style`.
Use ordinary CSS or the flex utility classes for other adjustments such
as centring a cluster with `justify-content`. None of the layout rules
sets a background, border, padding, or outer margin.
